title: SIEM export - Audit & RBAC v2 field contracts and evidence automation
content:
Purpose
This note defines a compact, deployable field-contract and transformation guidance for SIEM exports (Splunk, Datadog, Azure Sentinel) that preserves RBAC v2 attributes and audit-evidence metadata for downstream compliance automation. It is intended for the customer integrations team and SREs building adapters.

Scope
- Source systems: Redwood inference control plane and private telemetry bridge.
- Targets: Splunk HEC, Datadog logs intake, Azure Sentinel (Log Analytics workspace via Data Collector API).
- Focus: audit log schema alignment, RBAC v2 attribute propagation, event-level evidence tokens, and lightweight envelope transforms.
- Excludes: agent-side collection (assumes telemetry forwarded to Redwood bridge).

Design goals and assumptions
- Preserve audit semantic: who, what, when, where, why.
- Avoid PII leakage: default redaction and explicit allow-list for customer-supplied fields.
- Compatible with downstream evidence automation that expects an "evidence_id" and immutable event digest.
- Minimal per-event overhead: additional envelope fields limited to 5–8 top-level keys.

Field contract (canonical event envelope)
Top-level fields (required):
- event_id: stable UUID v4 for the event.
- event_time: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp (rfc3339).
- event_type: short string (audit.login, audit.model_deploy, access.granted, config.change).
- actor: principal identifier (format: type:id; e.g., user:alice@example.com or service:dedicated-123).
- actor_roles: list string (comma-separated if target system doesn't support arrays) containing RBAC v2 roles at time-of-event.
- resource: short resource descriptor (type:id; e.g., model:rw-instruct-v2).
- outcome: success | failure | throttled | partial.
- evidence_id: opaque token linking to evidence bundle (GUID).
- event_digest: SHA256 hex of canonical payload (used to detect tampering).
- context: optional free-form JSON string (must be base64 encoded when passing to Datadog to avoid truncation).

Recommended optional fields:
- client_ip: redacted by default (retain last octet masked) unless customer allows full IP.
- request_id: upstream request trace id for correlation with traces.
- region: logical region/cluster id.
- retention_tag: compliance label (e.g., pii-low, audit-high).

RBAC v2 considerations
- Policy snapshot vs effective roles: Include actor_roles as effective roles; include linked_policy_id if available to allow reconciliation.
- Minimal trust: do not embed role definitions in event. Reference policy ids only (policy:uuid).
- Temporal validity: attach role_valid_from and role_valid_to when roles are scoped to a session.

Audit log schema mapping for SIEM targets
- Splunk HEC: send canonical envelope as a single JSON event. Use top-level keys as Splunk event fields. For arrays (actor_roles), convert to CSV string. Ensure event_digest is indexed but context kept in _raw only. HEC header "X-Splunk-Request-Channel" should carry evidence_id for routing.
- Datadog Logs: Datadog treats long JSON fields poorly; put the canonical envelope under "message" for human-readable events and use tags for fast-filters: dd.env, dd.region, actor, event_type. For evidence_id and event_digest, set as attributes (attributes.evidence_id, attributes.event_digest). Base64-encode context when more than 4k chars.
- Azure Sentinel (Log Analytics): map canonical envelope into the custom log schema (RedwoodAudit_CL). Field suffix must be _s for string fields and _t for datetime (e.g., event_time_t). Use evidence_id_s, actor_s, resource_s, event_type_s, event_digest_s.

Sample payloads
- Splunk (HEC payload)
{
  "event_id": "b3f2f2b6-8a1e-4d5d-9b3e-11a9a7efc1d0",
  "event_time": "2025-02-18T15:42:12Z",
  "event_type": "audit.model_deploy",
  "actor": "user:maya@redwood.com",
  "actor_roles": "platform-admin,model-publisher",
  "resource": "model:rw-instruct-v2",
  "outcome": "success",
  "evidence_id": "ev-20250218-6a7f3",
  "event_digest": "f2c9e2f6... (sha256)",
  "context": "{\"git_ref\":\"main\"}"
}

- Datadog (recommended attribute mapping)
message: Compact audit: "audit.model_deploy by maya@redwood.com outcome=success model=rw-instruct-v2"
attributes.evidence_id: ev-20250218-6a7f3
attributes.event_digest: f2c9e2f6...
tags: ["env:prod","region:us-west-2","event_type:audit.model_deploy"]

- Sentinel (Log Analytics)
RedwoodAudit_CL
| event_id_s = b3f2f2b6-8a1e-4d5d-9b3e-11a9a7efc1d0
| event_time_t = 2025-02-18T15:42:12Z
| event_type_s = audit.model_deploy
| actor_s = user:maya@redwood.com
| actor_roles_s = platform-admin,model-publisher
| resource_s = model:rw-instruct-v2
| outcome_s = success
| evidence_id_s = ev-20250218-6a7f3
| event_digest_s = f2c9e2f6...

Evidence automation hooks (how downstream systems will use fields)
- evidence_id: primary key for the evidence automation orchestrator. When present, connectors must ensure it is passed verbatim to the evidence service API.
- event_digest: used for immutability verification. The evidence service will reject bundles where digest mismatch is detected.
- retention_tag: drives retention policy; evidence automation will move bundles to cold storage for tags matching audit-high + 7y.
- actor_roles and linked_policy_id: used by compliance checks to validate whether an action was permitted at the time-of-event.

Connector transform rules and implementation notes
- Implement transforms as stateless mapping functions in the telemetry bridge: canonicalize -> redact -> enrich -> encode-for-target. Keep transform configs in YAML with a version.
- Default redaction rules: email -> hash(email) unless allowlist:true. full IP -> redact to x.x.x.0.
- Backpressure handling: if target rejects large context fields, emit truncated context and set context_truncated=true in the envelope. Log the truncation event to the internal debug index.
- Metrics: per-connector counters for accepted, rejected, truncated, mapped_events, evidence_missing.

Customer requirements checklist (what we send customers before integration)
- Delivery SLA (events per minute, burst tolerance).
- Retention class mapping and any special export windows.
- PII policy: which fields may be unmasked.
- Required indexing fields on customer SIEM side (e.g., event_type, evidence_id).
- Credentials and rotation plan for HEC/API keys or Workspace ID/Primary key.

Migration and compatibility notes
- Back-compat: allow consumer to accept older envelope version v1 where event_digest might be absent. Version field should be present: envelope_version: v2.
- Rolling upgrade: dual-write to old schema and v2 for 30 days during major changes.

Operational runbook (high-level)
- On ingestion errors: attempt 3 retries with exponential backoff; on persistent failure, drop event to dead-letter queue with reason and evidence_id. Notify on-call if >100 failed events in 1 minute.
- Tamper detection: evidence service flags digest mismatch -> open incident and automatically suspend writes for actor for 5 minutes pending investigation.

Open questions / action items
- Decide default lifetime for evidence tokens (ev-*) and whether they should be monotonically increasing or time-encoded. (owner: Priya)
- Confirm Datadog context encoding approach to avoid UI truncation. (owner: Daniel)
- Verify legal team's retention thresholds for cross-border evidence replication. (owner: Omar)

Appendix: quick reference mapping table
- event_id -> Splunk:event_id, Datadog:attributes.event_id, Sentinel:event_id_s
- actor_roles -> Splunk:actor_roles (CSV), Datadog:tags, Sentinel:actor_roles_s
- evidence_id -> indexed key across all targets

Notes on uniqueness and partial overlaps
This doc intentionally focuses on the "contract" surface (field names, small envelope, evidence hooks) rather than on full onboarding flows or adapter reliability patterns covered in other collateral. Use this as the canonical field-level spec to include in customer-facing integration agreements and attach to connector PRs.
